string.text: Master switch for every effect in this mod on this computer.

Turns gore off at once on this computer: blood on walls, floors and bodies, blood sprays, pools, severed parts, gibs and stumps disappear, including what is already there, and no new gore appears. With baked models, bodies missing limbs get them back. Explosions, sparks, dust and debris stay, and nothing about the game itself changes. Untick it and everything comes back. In co-op it only changes your own screen.
Kid mode: hide particles already flying (experimental)

Also hides blood sprays and gore debris that are already on screen when kid mode goes on, and the ones the game plays by itself (knife hits on flesh, anomalies tearing a body), by switching their particle shader off. Needs the xrRazom exe's shader bus and DirectX 10 or 11, and is not tested in game yet. Off: those particles finish playing as usual.
Hits between NPCs near you (see Performance -> Detail distance) also paint blood and play effects. Dismemberment stays limited to players' kills and explosions. In co-op the host's setting applies.
One line in the game log for every body an explosion reaches: distance, damage, fragments and what came off. Useful for bug reports; costs nothing noticeable.
Writes detailed [ZGO] lines to the game log. Only for tracking down problems: it makes the log large.
Pick a preset for your machine, then fine-tune any slider. Each player sets this for their own computer.

Sets every slider on this page for a kind of machine: Potato for very weak PCs and old laptops, Low, Medium, High (the default, tuned on a mid-range gaming PC) and Ultra for strong PCs. You can still move any slider afterwards; nothing changes until you press Accept.
How long blood stays on walls, floors and bodies before it fades. A lot of blood on screen at once costs some GPU time.
Most blood streams traced through the air for one hit. Each one costs a few ray casts and a decal; lower it if big fights stutter.
How many wounds on the living can spread their stain at the same time; past this the oldest stops spreading. 0 = wounds don't spread.
Above this rate, effects that aren't essential are skipped (also for effects a co-op host sends you). Scaled by Particles -> Intensity.
Hard limit for this mod's particle effects playing at the same moment; the oldest make room for new ones.
Severed parts and gibs at once
Pieces flying or lying around; past this the oldest resting piece is removed. Each flying piece runs a little physics. 0 = none stay.
Severed parts: time on the ground (s)
Seconds before a severed part or gib is removed.
Pieces farther than this from you are removed.

How far from you NPC-vs-NPC fights and NPC explosions get full blood and gore, and (a little further) how far blood trails and death pools are drawn. Your own and your co-op partners' kills always get everything.
How many bodies an explosion's gore is worked out for in one frame; the rest follow in the next frames. Higher puts everything in the same frame (a bigger hitch).
How many queued hits and co-op effects are handled each frame. Lower spreads the work out: smoother, effects a little later.
Most impact marks this mod paints per second; in heavy fire the rest are skipped (the game's own bullet holes still appear). Marks are cheap to keep but each costs a ray cast to place.
Seconds before an impact mark or a crater's scorch fades. Many marks on screen at once cost some GPU time. Marks are never kept in saves.
World impacts: dust and sparks per second
Most dust puffs, chips and spark effects started per second; above this the rest are skipped. Explosion dust and smoke always play.
Impacts and explosions farther than this from you (or, on a co-op host, from every player) get no marks or dust from this mod.
How many spots on walls and floors keep their built-up damage; past this the spot hit longest ago starts from scratch. Costs a little memory and nothing per frame.
World impacts: rubble and clods at once
Clods, chunks and crater rims lying around at once; the oldest goes first. Each flying piece runs a little physics. 0 = none.
How long smoke hangs over a crater. Large soft smoke costs GPU time when you stand in it. 0 = no lingering smoke.
Most dust, splinter, spark and glass effects from objects per second (also for those a co-op host sends you); past it, hits on objects show only the game's own effect.
Pieces of broken objects at once

Pieces of broken crates, chairs and bottles flying or lying around; past this the oldest resting piece is removed. Each flying piece runs a little physics. 0 = objects vanish in a burst of dust instead.
Seconds before a piece of a broken object is removed.
Barrels and canisters leaking at the same time; a new leak beyond this stops the oldest. Each leak plays a stream and places a few puddle marks.
Hits, leaks and breaks farther than this from you show no extra effects (objects still break; the pieces are just not drawn).
How long puddles from leaking containers stay on the floor.
How many wounded bodies near you draw their wounds as craters (Wounds -> Wound craters, experimental); the rest keep their wound marks only. Each one costs a little GPU time while it is on screen.
How many separate wounds one body keeps track of; past this the lightest one is forgotten (its marks stay). At most four of them per body part are drawn as craters.
How often the bodies drawing wound craters are chosen again as you move, and wounds shared by a co-op host are put on bodies. Higher reacts faster and costs a little more CPU.
Bodies with broken limbs at once

Most bodies the native bone hooks bend at the same time (newest first; older ones go back to normal). Each costs a little CPU every frame it is drawn. Only matters with Native extensions -> Bone hooks on. 0 = none.
In co-op the host's settings on this page apply to everyone.
Scales how many blood streams each hit throws and how big they land.
Entry and exit wounds and blood stains on the victim.
Streams that fly into another person stain them.
The wounded leave drops and trails as they move, following the game's own bleeding.
Wet blood on walls runs down over a few seconds.
In co-op the host's settings on this page apply to everyone.
Hit sprays, exit wounds, head bursts, sparks and gore debris from this mod.
Scales how many particle effects may play per second (see Performance).
Pulsing spurts from neck and artery hits; stumps gush after dismemberment.
Sparks and armour fragments when rounds are stopped by armour or helmets.
In co-op the host's settings on this page apply to everyone.
Heads and limbs can come off on kills and when shooting bodies. The chance depends on calibre and on damage built up on the body part.
Limbs come off from the hit bone downward.
Bodies keep taking damage; enough rifle rounds into a limb takes it off.
Multiplies every dismemberment chance (2 = twice as likely).
The severed part flies off and tumbles to the ground. They are not kept in saves.
Chunks thrown by head bursts and explosions: torn-out pieces of the body itself, or meat models (see Gib look).

What an explosion or a head burst throws. Pieces of the body: chunks torn out of that body's own model, with its clothes, skin or fur on the outside and raw flesh underneath; each one flies off from the spot it came from, the ones nearest the blast first. ZGO Setup makes them with the baked models (README, BAKED MODELS; a bake from 1.7.1 or newer, about 0.2 MB per body model). A body without them, or wearing a model another mod replaced after the bake, throws meat models. Meat models: G.A.M.M.A.'s mutant meat items, as before. To check: throw a grenade at a body with Pieces of the body: the pieces must wear the body's own clothes and fly out from where they were. If the game shows an error about a model, pick Meat models and report it. Each player's own setting.
Direct RPG hits and IEDs going off underfoot take the whole body apart. Grenades, launcher rounds and mines take limbs, never whole bodies.

Uses the cut-ready character models made by the model baker (see README, BAKED MODELS): limbs come off corpses too, and late blasts still take parts. Off: behaves as if they were not installed (they stay loaded). Each player's own setting.

What closes a stump where a part came off. Meat disk: a slab of raw meat over the cut, as before. Fitted to the cut (experimental): the cap the model baker made for that body and that cut (README, BAKED MODELS), flesh and a broken bone shaped exactly like the wound; it bends with the body. Fitted, fixed to the joint (experimental): the same cap held still on the joint above the cut, in case the first one looks wrong in your game. Inside the model (experimental): the caps that a bake with --experimental-caps puts inside every model, shown through the off shader (needs Cut with the off shader); without them the fitted caps are used. Fitted caps need a bake from version 1.7; without one, or on a body whose model another mod replaced, the meat disk is used. To check: pick a fitted shape and shoot a forearm and a thigh off a body: a fleshy cap with a bone stub must close the stump without a gap, also while the body moves. If the game shows an error about a model, or a cap floats away from the body, go back to Meat disk and report it. Each player's own setting.

A severed limb is drawn with the model baker's piece of that body (only the part that came off, with a closed, fleshy end) instead of a copy of the whole body with everything else shrunk away: lighter to draw, and no open hole at the cut. Needs a bake from version 1.7 with pieces (README, BAKED MODELS); without one, or on a body whose model another mod replaced, nothing changes. Experimental: the piece models have not been checked in the game yet. To check: tick it and shoot an arm off a body: the arm must fly off from where it was, look the same as on the body and show a closed end; if the hand had been shot off before, it is missing from the piece too. If the game shows an error about a model, untick it and report it. Each player's own setting.

With baked models, a part that comes off is switched off by this mod's own shader (zgo\off) instead of by hiding its bones while the body falls: the joint above the cut is never squeezed, a part can come off before the body has fallen, and every cut shows at once. Bones are still hidden once the body lies as a ragdoll, so bullets and blood marks don't land on the missing part. Needs a bake from version 1.7 (README, BAKED MODELS); bodies without it, or wearing another mod's model, are cut as before. Experimental: first run probe 1 (Off shader) on the Diagnostics page; the part must vanish cleanly. Then tick this and shoot limbs and heads off a few NPCs and bodies: each part must vanish at once with its shadow, with no stretched skin at the joint; save and load: the parts stay off. If a part comes back, the wrong part vanishes or a joint looks squeezed, untick it and report it. Each player's own setting.

ZGO Setup (in the ZGO folder: tools\zgo_setup) bakes the body models for your own mod list. These options only decide what the game tells you about that bake. Each player sets them for their own computer.
Check the bake when a game loads

A few seconds after a save loads, compares your baked models with what the game really loads, and tells you once per problem (a message on screen and a line in the log) when ZGO Setup should be run again or a mod in MO2 hides baked models: a newer ZGO, changed body-part tables, models replaced by a mod that loads after ZGO, missing files. It only reads, spread over the first second; off = no check at all.
Remind me when nothing is baked
If no models are baked, says once per ZGO version that running ZGO Setup gives cleaner cuts on bodies. ZGO also works without a bake, with the limits described in the README (BAKED MODELS).
Also look at the other mods' files (experimental)

Also reads MO2's mod list and the model files the bake was made from, straight from the MO2 folder (under Proton through drive Z:), so the message can name the mod that was added, removed, reordered or updated. Experimental: whether the game may read MO2's folders this way is not checked in the game yet; if it cannot, the log says so once and nothing else happens. Costs a few thousand file look-ups spread over a few seconds after loading.
Runs the check as soon as you close the menu and shows the result, even if it was shown before (also when everything is fine).

Damage builds up where bodies are hit: a bruise, an open wound, a crater, down to the bone, until the part comes off. Needs the baked models from bake.py 1.7 or later (see README, BAKED MODELS). In co-op the host's settings on this page apply to everyone, except the ones marked as your own.

Every hit adds damage to the nearest wound spot on the body, scaled by calibre: a pistol round bruises and opens wounds, a rifle round tears, an anti-materiel round or a slug craters at once. Enough hits on one spot go through the stages: bruise, open wound, crater, down to the bone, and finally the part comes off. Works on the living and on bodies, on people and mutants that have baked models with wound sites (bake.py 1.7 or later). Without them nothing changes.
Multiplies the damage each hit adds to a wound. 2 = half as many hits to reach a crater or the bone, 0.5 = twice as many.
Deep wounds show on the body
When a wound reaches a crater, the bone or worse, a larger torn wound mark is painted on the body there, on top of the usual entry and exit marks. Lighter wounds look as before.

A wound that reaches a crater or deeper throws a few meat chunks out of the body; more at the bone and when the part is destroyed. Uses the same meat models and limits as Dismemberment -> Gibs (which must also be on) and Performance -> Severed parts and gibs at once.

When a wound on a dead body's head, arm or leg is destroyed (the last stage), that part comes off, following the Dismemberment settings (heads, limbs, mutants, shooting bodies). The living never lose parts.
Wound craters in the body (experimental, your own)

Wounds become real holes in the body's surface: a crater with a bloody rim, layers of fat and muscle on the walls and bone at the bottom of the deepest ones, which move with the body and its shadow. Experimental: it needs models baked with bake.py --experimental-damage (much larger), the DirectX 10 or 11 renderer, and shader features not yet confirmed in this game. To check it: first run Diagnostics probes 1, 2 and 3 (they must pass), save, tick this, then shoot one spot on a body several times with a rifle; a crater should open there, and the body should look exactly as before everywhere else, shadow included. If the game closes, parts of bodies vanish or flicker, or bodies turn pink, untick it and report it. Each player's own setting; partners see their own setting.
In co-op the host's settings on this page apply to everyone.

G.A.M.M.A. armour subtracts its whole explosion protection from a blast, so NPCs could shrug off a grenade at their feet. With this on, the blast does at least what its overpressure would: a hand grenade within about a metre kills most people, at 2 m it hurts, at 3 m it barely does. Armour cuts it (an exoskeleton by about a third), walls in between cut it more. Story characters other mods protect are left alone.
Scales the realistic blast damage above. 1 = the tuned values.

G.A.M.M.A. No NPC Friendly Fire also cancels the blast and shrapnel of an NPC grenade on its own side, so it only ever hurt its target. With this on, explosions hurt everyone near them; bullets are still filtered and relations still patched, so allies caught in a blast stay allies.

Objects in the world: what bullets and explosions do to crates, barrels, bottles, lamps and furniture. In co-op the host's settings on this page apply to everyone, except the effects and sounds each player sees and hears. Kid mode does not change any of it.
Master switch for everything on this page. Off: objects behave exactly as in the game without this mod.

Bullets throw material-specific bits off what they hit: wood splinters and dust, sparks from metal, glass shards, paper and cloth fluff, chips from plastic and ceramics. Adds to the game's own impact effects. Each player's own setting.

How much harder bullets shove loose objects, on top of the game's own push. Heavier rounds push more, heavy objects move less. 0 = only the game's own push. In co-op the host applies it once, so everyone sees the same motion.
Explosions lift and spin loose objects near them instead of only sliding them. 0 = only the game's own push.

A bullet hole in a barrel, canister or milk can below its fill line leaks: a stream and a growing puddle (water, fuel, oil or chemicals, depending on the container) until it has run dry. Gas bottles and fire extinguishers hiss out a jet instead.
When a crate, board, fence or jar the game itself can break comes apart, it bursts with dust, splinters or glass sized to the object, with a crack. Each player's own setting.
Shooting a hanging lamp throws glass and sparks; a lamp that survives a hit may flicker for a moment, a lamp that goes out showers shards.

Small crates, chairs, stools, bottles and jars that the game can't break wear down under fire and explosions and come apart into pieces; barrels and milk cans too, once the setup tool has cut their pieces (its Breakable objects step). Only objects with a matching set of pieces break (see README, PROPS); quest items, stashes, doors and anything with its own script never do. A broken object stays gone after a reload.
Multiplies how much damage it takes to break an object. 2 = twice as many hits; 0.5 = half.
Knife and other melee hits count toward breaking the objects above (only those the game reports hits on: small crates and similar).
Bottles, jars and other glass objects near an explosion shatter, and lamps the blast puts out shower glass. Window panes are part of the level and stay whole.
A crack, crash or shatter (the game's own material sounds) when an object breaks. Each player's own setting.
Bullet marks, dust and debris on walls, floors and objects, and craters from explosions. In co-op the host's settings on this page apply to everyone, except the ones marked as your own.

Rounds that hit walls, floors, trees and objects leave marks sized by calibre (a pistol chips, a rifle gouges, an anti-materiel round blows a crater) and throw dust, chips and sparks that match the surface. The game's own bullet holes stay; this adds to them. Off: only the game's own bullet holes.

Hits on the same spot add up: chips turn into cracks, then a deep gouge, and sustained fire knocks a dark breach into concrete, brick, plaster, wood and thin metal. Marks only: walls don't open and bullets don't pass through them.
Multiplies the size of every mark this page adds (bullet marks and craters). 1 = sized by calibre as tuned.
Dust, splinters and sparks also come off crates, barrels, cars and other objects that are not part of the level. No marks are painted on them (the game paints its own).
Rounds fired by NPCs near a player get the same marks and dust as yours. Off: only players' shots (yours and co-op partners').

Grenades, rockets, mines and IEDs leave a scorched crater sized by the charge, pock marks from fragments around it, a ring of dust that rolls out along the ground and smoke that hangs for a while. Indoors, grit and dust fall from the ceiling.

Explosions throw clods of earth or chunks of concrete that tumble and come to rest, and leave a low rim of thrown-up dirt or rubble around the crater. Visual only: nothing blocks movement or bullets, and nothing is kept in saves. The number at once is on the Performance page. Experimental: the pieces are new models of this mod. To check it: tick it and throw a grenade onto open ground; a ring of dirt should appear around the crater and a few clods should land around it. If the game shows an error about a model, untick it and report it.
Draw impact dust and sparks (your own)
Dust puffs, chips, splinters, sparks, crater dust and smoke on this computer. Off saves a little GPU time; marks and craters stay. Each player's own setting.

Draws impact marks with this mod's own decal shader: gouges and breaches look recessed (parallax), scorch is sooty and cracks get darker edges, and marks fade out smoothly with age. Experimental: it needs the shader file from this mod to load (see README, WORLD IMPACTS). To check it: tick it, shoot a concrete wall a few times; marks should look deeper than before. If they turn into flat grey squares or vanish, untick it and report it. Each player's own setting.

Optional engine add-on (bin\zgo_native.dll). Off by default; while it is off, nothing on this page loads or changes anything. It only works with the xrRazom game executables it recognises: on any other exe it stays off on its own and writes the reason to the log. Use "Write a status report to the log" to see what it found.
In co-op every player sets the first two switches for their own computer; a feature only runs when every player in the session has it working. The host decides the rest.

Loads bin\zgo_native.dll when a game starts. The DLL first checks that this exact game executable is one it knows (it looks for every engine function it needs and compares their code byte by byte); if anything differs it switches itself off and changes nothing. Loading alone changes nothing in the game either: each feature below has its own switch. Experimental: if the game crashes or behaves oddly with this on, switch it off and report it with your log.
Bone hooks: bend and crush bodies (experimental)

Installs three small engine hooks (after the skeleton update CalculateBones, in the bone lookup LL_BoneID, and where a model is released, Depart) so the mod can bend, crush or shift single bones of a body after the game has posed it: broken limbs and caved-in chests on bodies hit by explosions (below). Switching it off takes the hooks out at once and every body goes back to normal. Costs almost nothing for bodies it leaves alone. Check in game: blow up a body with a grenade; its arms or legs should bend at odd angles and stay that way while it ragdolls.

Bodies close to an explosion get limbs bent at broken angles, and with a heavy charge a crushed chest or a dislocated shoulder. Only bodies (never the living), only once the body has gone limp, and the same on every co-op machine. Needs the bone hooks above. Kid mode removes them.
How far limbs bend and how many break for the same explosion. 1 = as tuned; 2 = more limbs, sharper angles; 0.5 = only close blasts break anything.
Write a status report to the log

Writes what the native add-on found to the game log (lines starting with [ZGO] native): whether the DLL loaded, the engine functions it recognised and verified, which hooks are in, how many bodies it bends, and in co-op what every player supports. Attach it to bug reports.

Smoke tests for engine features that later versions of ZGO will rely on. Each button starts one probe as soon as you close the menu. It writes PASS, FAIL or MANUAL (judge it by eye) to the log and to appdata\zgo_probe_report.txt, shows on screen what to look for, and puts back everything it changed. A probe that needs something near you (a body, an NPC, a loose object) says so when there is none. Send the report file along with a bug report.
How long the probes that change something on screen (a shader, a model, kid mode) keep the change before putting it back, so you have time to look.

Probes 1, 2, 3 and 7 put ZGO's own shaders on bodies or swap a loose object's model: engine paths nobody has checked in the game yet. If one of the shaders does not compile, the game closes, so save first. Tick this, press Accept and open the menu again to see their buttons.
Runs probes 9, 4, 8 and 6 one after another (baked models, FFI, kid mode lane, co-op), then writes a summary. None of them leaves anything changed; probe 8 hides blood for a few seconds.

Stand 3-10 m from a living NPC and a body. Puts the zgo\off shader on one part (usually the head) of each for a few seconds: the part and its shadow must vanish cleanly, with no stretched skin, and come back. In kid mode the whole body vanishes instead.

Stand near several different NPCs or mutants (a base is ideal). For a few seconds their bodies are drawn with ZGO's copy of the game's skinned-model shader, chosen so all four skinning formats are covered: they must look exactly as before, shadows and motion included. The game closes if the shader does not compile.

Stand near two or three NPCs. For a few seconds each one gets its own number through the shader's textures: their torsos turn red, green and blue. Magenta or a missing torso means the numbers did not arrive. The game closes if the shader does not compile.
Checks that scripts can load LuaJIT's FFI and that the game's exe sits at the address the native add-on expects; asks the native add-on too when it is installed. Changes nothing.

Stand near bodies with parts cut off. Press, close the menu, save the game, load that save and wait 8 seconds: the probe checks that every recorded body came back with the same parts missing, in the same place.

In co-op, stand near some bodies (cut up is best). The host compares what every player's game shows of them (missing parts, ZGO shaders, gib and decal counts) and reports a match or mismatch per player. On a client the button asks the host. In single player it shows this machine's numbers only.

Single player. Stand next to a small loose object (bottle, can, small box). Swaps its model for another small one for a few seconds, then back: push it meanwhile, the new model must move with it. A save made meanwhile is put right when it is loaded.

Switches kid mode on for the blood shaders only, for a few seconds, and checks that the shader bus lane zgo_view goes 0, 1, 0: blood on walls and bodies must vanish and come back. Nothing else changes. Skipped while kid mode is on.

Stand near a few NPCs. Compares the number of parts their models have in the game with ZGO's bake: finds models another mod overrides (fix: ZGO higher in MO2, or bake again) and models the game loaded before the bake (fix: restart the game). Changes nothing.
For the probes you judge by eye: adds a line to the report saying the last one looked as described.
Adds a line to the report saying the last probe did not look as described; say what you saw in your bug report.
